question.problem:
A restaurant manager records the total time $20$ customers waited before they were seated. The results are presented in the table below. 

| Waiting time (minutes) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $4$ |
| $10\le x<15$ | $6$ |
| $15\le x<20$ | $7$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $3$ |

$$

$$

Assuming that the waiting times within each class interval are uniformly distributed, find an estimate of the mean waiting time $\overset{―}{x},$ rounded to **one decimal place**.

Rounded to one decimal place, $\overset{―}{x}≈$
{{field-1}} minutes.
question.worked_solution:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows:

$$
\overset{―}{x}≈\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{K}{f}_{i}\cdot {m}_{i}
$$

where

- ${f}_{i}$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

- ${m}_{i}$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

- $n$ is the total number of observations.

To estimate the mean, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each class and the products of the midpoints and frequencies.

| Waiting time (minutes) | ${f}_{i}$ | ${m}_{i}$ | ${f}_{i}\cdot {m}_{i}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0\le x<10$ | $4$ | $5$ | $20$ |
| $10\le x<15$ | $6$ | $12.5$ | $75$ |
| $15\le x<20$ | $7$ | $17.5$ | $122.5$ |
| $20\le x<30$ | $3$ | $25$ | $75$ |

$$

$$

Finally, we sum the values in the last column and divide by $20$ (the total number of observations).

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & ≈\frac{20+75+122.5+75}{20} \\  & =\frac{292.5}{20} \\  & ≈14.6\end{aligned}
$$
